prompts:
Use case: illustration-story. Generate ONE standalone 16:9 horizontal Chinese article illustration, not a sheet of multiple illustrations. Intended final 1280x720. Pure RGB white (#FFFFFF) background, minimalist black hand-drawn pen linework, gently irregular thin lines, sparse flat red/orange/blue accents, substantial white margins and at least 45% empty white space. Main content within middle 80% width and 65% height. No shading, no gray wash, no gradients, no shadows, no texture, no dense UI, no commercial vector art, no PPT slide, no infographic boxes or title at upper left, no childish/cute mascot poster. Serious, unusual editorial product sketch.
Recurring character XiaoM: mushroom creature with RED rounded dome cap, 3–5 WHITE spots, black hand-drawn outline, small CREAM stem body, BLACK dot eyes, deadpan face, TWO thin arms and TWO thin legs. Never a solid black mushroom. XiaoM must DO the central action. Restrained Chinese handwritten labels only where explicitly listed, no other prose, no English except IK if requested. Orange only for change/movement arrows, blue only for review/secondary notes; black for objects and outlines. Keep readable spacious composition.
Theme: prove a tiny courtyard gameplay loop with blockout primitives BEFORE swapping in matching art, retaining the same interaction.
Composition: two small open isometric courtyard miniatures side by side on white, with identical ground dimensions, entrance, player/can/flower positions and path. Left: a low rectangular CUBE ground slab, a clearly geometric CAPSULE player with no humanoid detail, an upright watering can with obvious handle and spout to pick up, and a single flower in a pot as goal. A few orange footprint/movement marks link capsule -> can -> flower, with a small water droplet next to the flower to show the achievable watering goal. This is a proposed verified playable blockout, not a rendering of the original game. Right: same footprint but simple matching stylized courtyard art: paving lines on the slab, clothed small player in same place, same can and flower in same places, same orange footprint route. Keep art version sparse, not a lush garden. XiaoM stands between stages actively lowering a thin removable paving/art shell onto the right slab using exactly two hands, like a stagehand dressing a working miniature without moving its mechanism. Shell must not obscure the can, player or flower. One short orange transition arrow between courtyards. Same tiny blue pickup/interaction anchor marks at can base on both sides communicate unchanged interaction, without technical UI.
Text, verbatim: "先跑通" below left, "再换美术" below right, "交互不变" in blue on a short shared connecting underline below both. Within the left loop at most the three tiny handwritten black labels "走动" / "拾取" / "浇花". No other labels.
Do not show art generation first. Preserve capsule on LEFT clearly; do not replace it with another mushroom. XiaoM is the operator BETWEEN the two scenes, not the player. All objects fully visible. White background rather than gray panels.

Theme: an agent changes a scene through tools, then reviews same-camera screenshots AND separate actual gameplay feedback. Screenshots inspect visible layout, NOT evidence of collision or state correctness.
Composition: one sparse tabletop editing-and-review vignette, no screen UI. Left-middle XiaoM uses a large thin black wrench held in one hand to adjust the position of a small courtyard prop on a miniature scene slab; the other hand holds a short feedback note, showing it is actively both editing and reviewing. A tiny camera on tripod to the right of the scene has a small blue padlock at its tripod foot to communicate unchanged camera. Farther right are just TWO small side-by-side snapshot cards showing the SAME can, single flower and floor, identical angle, framing and object scale, with only the can placement slightly different before/after. The snapshot cards are hand-drawn visual records, not actual app screenshots. ONE simple blue leader from the cards back toward XiaoM indicates visual review. BELOW the scene, separate from the snapshot cards, a small game controller with orange footprints leading around a simple short wall and a pickup-can icon represents ACTUAL RUNNING PLAYTEST; a short curved blue feedback arrow leads from this controller test back to the note in XiaoM's hand. This gameplay path is visibly independent of camera snapshots.
Text, verbatim, exactly four small notes: "工具修改" near the wrench; "同机位" above the fixed camera/cards; "看外观" underneath the cards in blue; "碰撞靠试玩" beside the controller in red. Nothing else.
Never put a collision checkmark or success proof on screenshots, never connect photos directly to collision validation. No inspector panels, no code, no editor chrome, no dense arrows. Subject group occupies about 50% canvas, extensive blank white around it.

Theme: a simple watering-can lift. Distinguish hand grip/contact and single prop ownership, arm IK pose adjustment, and offline baked animation export. A baked clip does NOT provide runtime adaptive IK.
Composition: one main large XiaoM figure at center-left, with exactly TWO arms attached to its body, and TWO legs; no duplicated arms, no ghost limbs. One arm bends naturally at elbow and lifts a small watering can just above a low ledge. Its ONE holding hand has a clear thumb and several simple curved fingers WRAPPED AROUND the arched can handle, with the handle passing THROUGH the grip, fingers in front and thumb opposite. The can hangs below that grip, not beside an open hand. Other arm relaxed down alongside body and clearly visible, NOT touching can. The ledge is directly below the can with a short orange upward movement arrow in the free space, conveying lift after contact. A small blue target ring at the holding wrist and a blue dot near elbow, linked by one thin blue annotation leader, indicate IK adjusts the arm pose; these are external rig markers, not extra physical arms. A tiny black link/parent symbol at handle contact indicates one controlling hand/owner after grip.
At right, with generous white gap, a small paper flipbook strip showing ONLY three little WATERING CAN silhouettes rising at fixed successive heights, joined by short tick marks, followed by a plain file icon with a tiny outward orange arrow. This is a fixed recorded motion / offline export record, not a second character or new scene. No line from this file back to IK target, no feedback loop, no arbitrary prop adapting itself. Visually distinct annotation leaders point respectively to fingers/handle, arm target, and recorded flipbook.
Text, verbatim, exactly four short handwritten notes: "握紧·单一控制" next to handle contact in black, "IK调姿势" beside the wrist target in blue, "离线烘焙" above the flipbook in black, "固定动作" below the exported file in red.
No runtime adaptive claim, no runtime feedback arrows, no extra skeletons or hands, no floating/disembodied grip closeup, no mechanical tentacles, no overlapping arm poses, no source-code or editor UI. Clear contact anatomy is the priority. Keep large white top and bottom margins.
